memory.content: parse_timeout is total: it must never panic and always return a usable millisecond value. Any malformed input (bad digits, unknown suffix, overflow via saturating_mul) silently degrades to DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS. This means DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS must stay a sane, nonzero timeout — malformed config values map onto it at boot (load_timeout, startup_budget_ms) with no error surfaced to the operator, so changing the constant silently changes behavior for every typo'd config in production.

The suffix checks must keep their order: strip_suffix("ms") before strip_suffix('s'). Every "Nms" string also ends in 's', so if the branches were reordered, "500ms" would strip 's', fail to parse "500m" — and since the fallback is now silent (unwrap_or(DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS) instead of the old panic), all millisecond values would quietly become 30_000 ms with no crash to flag the regression. Only the unit tests guard this.
